item.title: How the Iran War Is Making Alaskans Both Richer and Poorer
item.description: Oil prices have surged across the United States as a result of the ongoing war in Iran. This means higher costs for households in most states, but in Alaska, the state government is bringing in new revenue from its high oil production to offset those higher costs. Some of the revenue is then redistributed to Alaskans through the state’s unique sovereign wealth fund. While most Americans disapprove of the war in Iran, Alaska may emerge as a quiet winner from one of the conflict’s most painful economic side effects: higher oil prices. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Protein Craze Fuels an Investment Boom in Livestock Health
item.description: Animal health companies are tapping into the protein craze, investing billions of dollars to build up businesses focused on making cattle, pigs and poultry healthier for human consumption.

item.title: Young Travelers Are Warming Up to Cruises
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News travel journalist Brittany Chang explains why cruises are attracting more Gen Z and millennial travelers as higher airfare and hotel costs make all-inclusive vacations increasingly appealing. Chang tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that cruise lines are courting younger passengers with mega ships, entertainment, adult-only spaces and nostalgia, with some sailings costing as little as about $30 a day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Economy and Democracy Drove the Blue Wave
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Rutgers University's Ashley Koning says affordability, concerns about democracy and government corruption helped drive voters toward Democrats, with significant shifts among Latino, young and independent voters. Koning tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Democrats now face pressure to deliver tangible results on affordability before the 2028 election cycle. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Berkshire Makes Record $9.6 Billion Buyback
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Insurance Analyst Matthew Palazola breaks down Berkshire Hathaway's third-quarter results, including a record $9.6 billion in share buybacks and weaker insurance earnings. Palazola tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that CEO Greg Abel is putting Berkshire's massive cash reserves to work through buybacks, acquisitions and equity investments while maintaining the measured approach associated with Warren Buffett. (Source: Bloomberg)
